## Summary

Methyl benzoate from benzoic acid. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Benzoic acid | 65-85-0 | 122.12 | 1.221 g | 10.0 | 1.0 |
| Sulfuric acid | 7664-93-9 | 98.07 | 0.1 mL | cat. | cat. |
| Methanol | 67-56-1 | 32.04 | 20 mL | – | – |
| Diethyl ether | 60-29-7 | 74.12 | 25 mL | – | – |
| Sodium hydrogen carbonate | 144-55-8 | 84.01 | saturated solution, 15 mL | – | – |
| Sodium sulfate | 7757-82-6 | 142.04 | 2 g | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Place benzoic acid and methanol in a flask.
2. Add sulfuric acid cautiously with stirring.
3. Fit a reflux condenser.
4. Heat at reflux for 2 hours.
5. Cool to room temperature.
6. Add water and transfer to a separatory funnel.

## Workup and Purification

Extract with diethyl ether (25 mL total). Wash the organic layer with saturated sodium hydrogen carbonate solution, venting frequently. Dry over sodium sulfate, filter and evaporate the ether.

## Characterization

Colourless liquid; IR (ATR): ester C=O near 1720 cm⁻¹. Expected ¹H NMR: δ 3.9 (s, 3H), 7.4–8.1 (m, 5H).

## Notes

1. Vent the funnel often during the carbonate wash because carbon dioxide is released.
2. Check the identity and purity of the product before further use.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Benzoic acid: causes serious eye damage; irritant; Sulfuric acid: causes severe burns; Methanol: highly flammable and toxic; causes organ damage; Diethyl ether: extremely flammable; forms explosive peroxides; Sodium hydrogen carbonate: dust may irritate eyes; Sodium sulfate: dust may irritate eyes; Methyl benzoate: harmful if swallowed. Work in a fume hood with gloves and eye protection. Collect aqueous and organic waste separately according to local rules.

## References

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R. Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th ed.; Longman: Harlow, 1989.
